capabilities.target: Any customer account record, looked up by email or account id

instructions.note: The agent may look up any customer by email or account id, not just the account of the person emailing it, with no technical restriction binding the lookup to the sender's identity.
The only safeguard against disclosing one customer's data to another is a prompt line ('Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you'), which is purely behavioral.

Escalation to a human ('unless the customer is angry') is left to the model's own sentiment judgment rather than a structural rule, so it is not a reliable gate and can be evaded by a calmly worded malicious request.

controls.name: Prompt rule: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model choosing to follow the instruction. A more capable or adversarially prompted model can rationalize an exception (e.g., 'the requester clearly already knows this account') or be convinced the disclosure is authorized.

controls.name: Escalate to a human when the customer is angry
controls.decay_rationale: The escalation trigger is a sentiment judgment made by the same model that is exposed to the untrusted email; it is not an externally enforced gate and can be avoided by calm, well-worded malicious requests.

controls.name: Bind CRM lookups to the verified sender identity
Raw-action human approval before sending cross-account PII
Recipient confirmation bound to the ticket's system-of-record requester
Least-privilege, per-request scoping of CRM and mail service credentials

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) with confused deputy (TC4): untrusted email drives unrestricted CRM lookup and unrestricted email send via shared service credentials

attack_path.note: Untrusted customer email arrives as a new ticket
Agent looks up any customer by email or account id using a broad CRM service token
Agent sends the looked-up data externally using a shared mail service account that can reach any address, with no human review

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version string changes without a separate review (subject.model.swappable is true), or the 'Never share another customer's information' prompt line is edited, removed, or weakened without security review.

evidence.observation: States the agent may look up their account with get_customer and 'may look up any customer by email or account id,' with no restriction to the sender's own account.
'If the answer is routine, send it directly with send. Do not wait for a human unless the customer is angry.' Sends are not gated by any structural approval mechanism.
'Never share another customer's information with the person emailing you.' is the only safeguard against cross-customer disclosure, and it is a prompt instruction.
Both crm_mcp and mail_mcp authenticate with a single static bearer token (CRM_SVC_TOKEN, MAIL_SVC_TOKEN).

'CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record.' and 'MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account. It can send to any address.' confirm broad, non-scoped credentials on both the read capability and the egress sink.
'Every outbound email is logged to the SIEM.' is detective only and runs after the email has already left the system, so it does not prevent the disclosure.

recommendations.action: Bind CRM lookups to the verified identity of the inbound requester; reject or hold for review any lookup of an account other than the sender's own.
Require a raw-action human approval gate before any outbound email contains PII for an account other than the requester's own.
Confirm the send destination against the ticket's system-of-record requester address rather than trusting a model-chosen recipient.
Replace the broad CRM_SVC_TOKEN and shared MAIL_SVC_TOKEN with least-privilege, per-request scoped credentials.

rating.rationale: A single present finding drives the rating: untrusted customer email can trigger an unrestricted CRM lookup of any account followed by an unrestricted external email send, using broad/shared service credentials (lethal trifecta plus confused deputy). Inherent is critical (U source to S3 sink: irreversible egress of confidential data). The only preventive controls are two behavioral, model-dependent instructions ('never share another customer's information' and an anger-triggered escalation), which earn one capped step-4 credit, giving a residual of high; SIEM logging is detective only and earns no tier credit. Because the sole credited control is dependent on model compliance, a model upgrade or an uncontrolled edit to the prompt removes that credit entirely, so the forecast returns to critical. The design lacks any structural control (scoped credentials, destination confirmation, or a raw-action approval gate) that would sever or durably narrow this path.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no execution traces, logs, or live tool responses were reviewed.
No explicit step or runtime limits are declared for autonomy, so max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are treated as unbounded (null), which is a conservative assumption.

Tool definition pinning or hash verification for crm_mcp and mail_mcp is not documented in the provided artifacts; definitions_pinned is assumed false pending confirmation from the MCP client configuration.
